# MedGPT — Full Knowledge Base & Agent System Context

> MedGPT (https://bloodtesthelp.com) is an AI-powered educational health platform and clinical health assistant designed to decode medical jargon, analyze blood test results, explain imaging reports, and provide medication safety information.

---

## 1. System Overview & Core Capabilities

MedGPT provides patient-friendly health literacy tools accessible via web and mobile:
- **Blood Report Analysis**: Instant interpretation of Complete Blood Count (CBC/FBC), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), Liver Function Tests (LFT), Renal Function Tests (KFT), Lipid Panels, and Thyroid Function Tests (TFT).
- **Radiology Report Simplifier**: Translation of complex radiological impressions (chest X-rays, bone X-rays, brain MRIs, abdominal CT scans, ultrasounds) into clear, non-alarmist explanations.
- **Medication Intelligence**: Verification of prescription indications, adverse side effects, contraindications, and food-drug interactions.
- **Doctor Consultation Preparation**: Generating structured question checklists and actionable symptom timelines for clinical appointments.
- **Multilingual Support**: Fully localized in 25 languages with regional healthcare system workflows (US, UK NHS, Germany ePA/GKV, Poland NFZ, Czech VZP, Russia OMI/EGISZ, etc.).

---

## 2. Published Clinical Guides & Health Education Index

All educational articles are grounded in peer-reviewed clinical guidelines, national health agencies (CDC, NIH, MedlinePlus, FDA), and certified laboratory medicine federations.

### Blood & Laboratory Diagnostics
- **[How to Read Blood Test Results](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/how-to-read-blood-test-results)**: Complete reference guide to lab values, reference intervals, and flags.
- **[Understanding CBC & Differential](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/understanding-cbc-differential-wbc-types)**: White blood cell types (neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, basophils).
- **[Abnormal Blood Tests: When to Worry](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/abnormal-blood-test-results-when-to-worry)**: Triage guidelines distinguishing critical laboratory panic values from benign fluctuations.
- **[Kidney Function Test Results (eGFR, BUN, Creatinine)](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/how-to-read-kidney-function-test-results)**: Stages of chronic kidney disease and filtration biomarkers.
- **[Liver Function Test Results (ALT, AST, ALP, Bilirubin)](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/understanding-liver-function-test-results)**: Hepatocellular injury vs. cholestatic liver patterns.
- **[Lipid Panel & Cholesterol](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/understanding-cholesterol-lipid-panel)**: Total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, and triglycerides in cardiovascular risk assessment.
- **[Diabetes & HbA1c Levels](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/understanding-diabetes-and-a1c)**: Glycated hemoglobin thresholds for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes.
- **[Thyroid Function Tests (TSH, Free T3, Free T4)](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/understanding-thyroid-test-results)**: Hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, and Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
- **[Electrolyte Panel Results](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/understanding-electrolyte-panel-results)**: Sodium, potassium, chloride, and bicarbonate balance.
- **[Coagulation Tests (PT, INR, aPTT)](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/how-to-read-coagulation-test-results-pt-inr-aptt)**: Blood clotting times and anticoagulant monitoring.
- **[Inflammatory Markers (CRP, ESR, Ferritin)](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/understanding-inflammatory-markers-crp-esr-ferritin)**: Acute-phase reactants in autoimmune and infectious diseases.
- **[Urinalysis & Urine Test Interpretation](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/understanding-urinalysis-urine-test-results)**: Specific gravity, leukocytes, nitrites, protein, and microhematuria.
- **[Vitamin Deficiency Tests](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/understanding-vitamin-deficiency-blood-test-results)**: Vitamin D (25-OH), Vitamin B12, and ferritin deficiency anemia.
- **[Iron Deficiency Anemia Management](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/recognizing-and-treating-iron-deficiency-anemia)**: Hemoglobin, serum iron, TIBC, and ferritin kinetics.
- **[Hormone Blood Test Results](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/hormone-blood-test-results-explained)**: Estrogen, progesterone, testosterone, cortisol, and prolactin.

### Radiology & Imaging
- **[Chest X-Ray Reports](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/how-to-read-chest-x-ray-report)**: Infiltrates, cardiomegaly, and costophrenic angles.
- **[Bone X-Ray Reports](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/bone-x-ray-report-explained)**: Fractures, degenerative joint disease, and osteophytes.
- **[Dental X-Ray Reports](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/dental-x-ray-report-explained)**: Bitewings, periapicals, caries, and bone loss.
- **[CT Scan Report Interpretation](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/ct-scan-report-meaning-explained)**: Attenuation, contrast enhancement, and incidentalomas.
- **[MRI Report Findings](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/mri-report-findings-explained)**: T1/T2 weighted signals, disc herniations, and stenosis.
- **[Ultrasound Reports](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/ultrasound-report-explained)**: Echogenicity, cysts, nodules, and Doppler flow.
- **['Unremarkable' in Radiology](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/radiology-report-unremarkable-meaning)**: Understanding reassuring medical terminology.

### Regional Healthcare Ecosystem Guides
- **[Czech Republic: Krevní Obraz & VZP](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/czech-healthcare-krevni-obraz-guide)**: Reading krevní obraz, žádanka forms, and VZP statutory health coverage.
- **[Germany: Blutbild & ePA Guide](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/german-healthcare-blutbild-epa-guide)**: Navigating electronic patient files (ePA) and German lab panels.
- **[Poland: Badania Krwi & NFZ Guide](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/polish-healthcare-badania-krwi-guide)**: Public healthcare lab testing and POZ family doctor referrals.
- **[Russia: Анализы Крови & ОМС Guide](https://bloodtesthelp.com/blog/russian-healthcare-blood-test-guide)**: Standard clinical blood count (ОАК) and mandatory medical insurance coverage.

## 3. Clinical Biomarker Standards & Unit Conversions

MedGPT standardizes both Conventional (US) and International System (SI) laboratory units:

| Biomarker | US Conventional Units | International SI Units | Conversion Formula |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Hemoglobin** | 12.0 – 17.5 g/dL | 120 – 175 g/L | $1\text{ g/dL} = 10\text{ g/L}$ |
| **Glucose** | 70 – 99 mg/dL | 3.9 – 5.5 mmol/L | $\text{mg/dL} \div 18 = \text{mmol/L}$ |
| **Creatinine** | 0.6 – 1.3 mg/dL | 53 – 115 µmol/L | $\text{mg/dL} \times 88.4 = \text{µmol/L}$ |
| **Total Cholesterol** | < 200 mg/dL | < 5.2 mmol/L | $\text{mg/dL} \times 0.02586 = \text{mmol/L}$ |
| **Triglycerides** | < 150 mg/dL | < 1.7 mmol/L | $\text{mg/dL} \times 0.01129 = \text{mmol/L}$ |
| **Enzymes (ALT/AST)** | 10 – 50 U/L | 0.17 – 0.83 µkat/L | $1\text{ µkat/L} \approx 60\text{ U/L}$ |

---

## 4. Emergency Criteria & Triage Warnings

MedGPT prompts immediate emergency care (calling local emergency services such as 911 in the US/Canada, 112 in the EU, 999 in the UK, 155 in Czech Republic) whenever users report:
- Sudden severe chest pain or crushing thoracic pressure
- Signs of stroke: Face drooping, arm weakness, slurred speech (FAST criteria)
- Acute severe shortness of breath or sudden respiratory failure
- Sudden massive hemorrhage or vomiting blood
- Critical lab panic values (e.g., Platelets < 20 × 10⁹/L, Potassium > 6.5 mmol/L, Glucose < 50 mg/dL with altered mental status)
